title: Scheduled Jobs dialog refresh storm: full grid rebuild plus one index.json disk read per job, on every scheduler event AND every 5 seconds, forever
existing_state: JobListDialog is modeless and single-instance (Form1.cs:166, 15171 via ModelessDialogManager.ShowOrActivate) so it commonly stays open all session. RefreshJobList runs from four triggers: a 5-second WinForms Timer (JobListDialog.cs:179-180) and full-refresh handlers for JobsChanged, JobStateChanged, and JobCompleted (433-435, 457-485). Each refresh clears and rebuilds the entire jobs grid (Rows.Clear at 502; the selection-preservation machinery at 566-606 exists only because of the rebuild) and, per job, calls GetLastResultText (755-763) -> JobHistoryService.GetRunsForJob(jobId, MaxResults=1) -> LoadJobIndex, an uncached File.ReadAllText + full JSON deserialize of that job's entire history index (up to 1000 entries with the editor's retention override) just to Take(1) (Services/JobHistoryService.cs:402-420, 499-518). It also re-parses every cron expression twice per job per refresh (CronExpressionDescriptor at JobListDialog.cs:724-732, Cronos at 734-753), and RefreshJobList then calls RefreshHistory (562, 642-718), which loads the selected job's same index file AGAIN and rebuilds the history grid — all synchronously on the UI thread. Because RunningState writes route through JobStorageService.Save, which fires JobsChanged (Services/JobStorageService.cs:138), and JobExecutionService fires JobStateChanged on every transition (Services/JobExecutionService.cs:904-906), a single run triggers at least five full refreshes. With a few dozen jobs and a busy scheduler that is hundreds of synchronous file reads, JSON parses, and cron parses per minute, plus 5-second grid rebuilds that wipe any column sort and cause visible repaint churn — and the 5-second poll is almost entirely redundant with the events.
recommendation: Make the event-driven path the only full refresh and demote the timer: (1) cache the last-run record per job in the dialog (Dictionary<jobId, JobRunRecord>), seeded once on open and updated from the JobCompleted event payload (JobRunResult already contains everything GetRunResultText needs), so GetLastResultText stops hitting disk; (2) coalesce the four triggers through a ~250ms one-shot debounce so event bursts produce one refresh; (3) have the 5-second tick only rewrite the Next Run cell values in existing rows instead of Rows.Clear + rebuild (or delete it). Optionally add a cheap JobHistoryService.GetLastRun(jobId) backed by an index cache invalidated on write — Form1's mirrored 5s scheduler status-bar timer benefits too.
user_benefit: Eliminates constant background disk I/O, JSON churn, and UI-thread work while the scheduler window sits open (it is modeless and often left open all day), keeps the window smooth during active runs, and stops the 5-second rebuild from wiping column sort.

evidence.note: 5s poll timer plus three event handlers all invoke full RefreshJobList
per refresh: both grids rebuilt, per-job GetLastResultText disk read, double cron re-parse, selected job's index loaded a second time
GetRunsForJob always reads and deserializes the whole index.json from disk, no caching
JobsChanged fires on every RunningState write, multiplying refreshes per run
dialog is modeless single-instance, so the poll runs for the life of the session
